headline: The account choices are right, but the business-savings procedure tells the agent to open the account with account_type 'savings' while the gold uses 'business_savings', and the two produce different accounts.

issues.summary: doc_004 (Opening Business Savings Accounts) instructs "Set account_type to 'savings'", while the tool docstring lists 'business_savings' and the gold uses it. With account_type 'savings' the tool runs the personal-savings eligibility check, which this customer passes (3-year personal Green checking), so the call succeeds and creates a different account id and record.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_004: "How to call: - Set account_type to 'savings'. - Set account_class to the exact official name provided by the customer (e.g., 'Bronze Saver Account')."
tools.py open_bank_account_4821 docstring: "Must be one of: 'checking' (personal checking), 'savings' (personal savings), 'business_checking', 'business_savings'"
replay: account_type "savings" -> "Bank account opened successfully! ... Account Type: savings"; verified match False, "table 'accounts' differs"
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that follows the internal business-savings procedure verbatim opens a "savings" account and fails the accounts table even though it chose the right product.
issues.suggested_fix: Change doc_004's tool instructions to "Set account_type to 'business_savings'".

issues.summary: Sky Blue is a startup account restricted to companies within 4 years of formation, and the customer script never says how old the business is. The promotion only applies among accounts the customer qualifies for, so the gold silently assumes eligibility.
evidence: doc_business_checking_accounts_sky_blue_001: "Confirm your company is within 4 years of formation."
doc_business_checking_accounts_sky_blue_008: "Eligibility criteria tied to company age are evaluated when you open the account; the threshold is 4."
user_scenario.instructions: no formation date or company age is given
issues.why_it_matters: A careful agent that asks the company age gets an improvised answer; if the simulated customer says more than 4 years, the agent correctly falls back to Lime Green and fails the gold. Most agents will not ask, so the effect is limited.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a line to the script stating the business was formed within the last 4 years (e.g., "I started the agency 2 years ago").

solution_check: Checking (mobile deposit >= $10,000/day, $0 overdraft fee, minimum < $10,000, APY >= 1%): Sky Blue ($25,000, $0, none, 1.25%), Lime Green ($15,000, $0, $5,000, 1.5%), Hunter Green ($10,000, $0, $5,000, 1.0%); November promotion puts Sky Blue first. Savings (same-day ACH, minimum < $50,000, wire <= $15): Gold Saver (Yes, 15), Silver Plus Saver (Yes, $5,000 min, 15), Gold Plus Saver (Yes, $25,000 min, $10); November promotion puts Gold Saver first. Business-savings eligibility holds (Cobalt Blue opened 09/15/2025, 60 days, $12,500). Gold matches; order of the two opens does not matter (replayed).
prior_note: Prior review rated the task clean; the account_type contradiction and the company-age gap were not reported there.
notes: Grading-model facts confirmed against the snapshot: gold replay + hash compare (evaluator_env.py); read logging only for gold-named discoverable reads (_derive_read_log_allowlist, call_discoverable_agent_tool); parse_int=float on discoverable args; apply_for_credit_card casts annual_income to float. Verified scorer (working-repo _verified_db_match) compares agent_discoverable_tools by tool-name set only and strips accounts.closure_reason; all other tables exact. Replays used the grep_only retrieval variant (no embeddings needed) with the gold-derived allowlist. The same doc_004 instruction affects any sibling task that opens a business savings account (e.g., task_056, outside this batch). Gold requires get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 (replay: skipping it fails).
